name: Coprinus comatus

size_cm.source: Kuo M 2008, Coprinus comatus: the shaggy mane, MushroomExpert.Com
size_cm.note: cap 3 to 15 cm; stem 5 to 20 cm long and 1 to 2 cm thick

notes: The cap digests itself into ink to release its spores, and it pushes up through asphalt. Reported (unchecked) to attack nematodes; cultivated.

tip_speed.note: Best strain (GMCC 67001) reached 63 mm on PDA after 9 days at 26 C from a 5 mm plug (Jang M-J, Lee Y-H, Liu J-J, Ju Y-C 2009, Optimal conditions for the mycelial growth of Coprinus comatus strains, Mycobiology 37(2):103-108, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3749398). Taken as colony diameter: (63 - 5) / 2 / 9 = 3.2 mm/day radius = 134 um/h. The paper does not say whether 63 mm is a diameter; if it were a radius the rate would be about 290 um/h. Per-temperature values are in a table image that could not be read

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

t_opt.source: Jang M-J, Lee Y-H, Liu J-J, Ju Y-C 2009, Optimal conditions for the mycelial growth of Coprinus comatus strains, Mycobiology 37(2):103-108
t_opt.note: Seven strains on PDA at 17, 20, 23, 26, 29 and 32 C for 9 days: best range 23 to 26 C, authors chose 26 C; poor growth above 29 C and below 20 C. A second study (Chaiyama et al. 2007, Songklanakarin J Sci Technol 29:261-274, seen only as a search snippet) gives 25 C on malt extract agar

cold_drop.note: Spawn supplier's growing sheet, not a peer-reviewed measurement: incubation room 21 to 27 C, then a night-time temperature of 18 to 24 C as a shock to start primordia (Mycelia NV, M8102 Coprinus comatus, https://mycelia.be/?p=3732). 3 C is the difference between the two ranges
